summary: SLD views: a cable inserted in one view is missing from the other views that contain both assets, so those views show the assets as not connected
desc:
h3. Simple explanation
A one-line diagram can have several views. A user inserts a cable on a connection while working in one view (view A).
The new cable and its node bus appear only in view A.
Another view (view B) that also shows both connected assets does not get the cable, so view B shows the two assets with no connection at all.
Anyone working in view B now sees a wrong diagram: a real connection looks missing.
ZP-4947 says an inserted cable must also reach the other views that hold both ends. It should show there too: asset → node bus → cable → asset.

!QA-12Nov-bugA-video-steps.mp4|width=640!
_Video (from the ZP-4947 test): Insert Cable in view A, then view B left unconnected, re-proved on a second pair._

!QA-12Nov-bugA-1-view-a-cable-inserted.png|width=640!
_1. View A after Insert Cable: XFMR-1 → node bus → cable → PNL-3 (red box)._

!QA-12Nov-bugA-2-view-b-not-connected.png|width=640!
_2. View B (also holds XFMR-1 and PNL-3): the two are NOT connected (red box)._

h3. Actual result
Only view A gets the new node bus and cable. View B shows XFMR-1 and PNL-3 with no connection, also after a reload 15 minutes later.

h3. Expected result
Every view that holds both ends of the connection shows the new node bus and cable, at the same layout offset as All Nodes.

h3. Test data
* Environment: QA (https://acme.qa.egalvanic.ai), Web v2.6, build index-C1ZRIunF.js, 12 Nov 2026, Super Admin seat.
* Site: "QA-DEMO v2.6 SLD editing 12 Nov" (SLD id c4438cd3-59b3-4639-9e60-2752dc5aa478), Engineering › SLD.
* Views: "QA-DEMO ZP-4947 view A 12 Nov" and "QA-DEMO ZP-4947 view B 12 Nov". Both contain QA26 XFMR-1 and QA26 PNL-3 (and later QA26 FUSE nosub and QA26 Load-1).

h3. Steps to reproduce
# Engineering › SLD on the site above. Make sure two views (A and B) both contain XFMR-1 and PNL-3, which are directly connected.
# In view A, unlock, right-click the XFMR-1 → PNL-3 connection › Insert Cable (screenshot 1).
# Open view B (screenshot 2): XFMR-1 and PNL-3 have no connection.
# Repeat on FUSE nosub → Load-1 (both added to view B first): same result (screenshots 3 and 4).

!QA-12Nov-bugA-3-reproof-view-a-fuse-load.png|width=640!
_3. Re-proof, view A: cable inserted on FUSE nosub → Load-1._

!QA-12Nov-bugA-4-reproof-view-b-not-connected.png|width=640!
_4. Re-proof, view B: FUSE nosub and Load-1 left unconnected._

h3. Notes for the developer
Insert Cable calls POST /api/edge/resolve-impedance-insertion and then adds the new nodes to the current view only. The view pass-through rule seems to place a new node into a view only when two of its neighbours are already there. With a node bus + cable chain, each new node has just one neighbour in view B, so neither is placed. Found while testing ZP-4947 (re-proved twice: 16:55 and 17:01 IST).

summary: SLD view: Delete › "Remove from View" leaves the asset's cable hanging in the view, while right-click › Remove from View removes both
desc:
h3. Simple explanation
In an SLD view there are two ways to remove an asset from the view.
Right-click the asset › Remove from View removes the asset AND the cable that would be left hanging. This is correct.
Select the asset › toolbar Delete › "Remove from View" removes only the asset. Its cable stays in the view with nothing on one end, and a hidden cable stays too.
The same action gives two different results, and the view is left with stray cables. Low priority.

!QA-12Nov-bugB-video-steps.mp4|width=640!
_Video (from the ZP-4947 test): the remove-from-view steps are at the end._

!QA-12Nov-bugB-1-cable-left-after-toolbar-remove.png|width=640!
_1. View B after toolbar Delete › Remove from View on PNL-1: its cable CBL-3 is still there (red box)._

h3. Actual result
Only the selected asset leaves the view. The cable next to it stays, with one end connected to nothing.

h3. Expected result
The same as right-click › Remove from View: the stranded cable is removed from the view too.

h3. Test data
* Environment: QA (https://acme.qa.egalvanic.ai), Web v2.6, build index-C1ZRIunF.js, 12 Nov 2026, Super Admin seat.
* Site: "QA-DEMO v2.6 SLD editing 12 Nov" (SLD id c4438cd3-59b3-4639-9e60-2752dc5aa478), Engineering › SLD.
* View: "QA-DEMO ZP-4947 view B 12 Nov" (PNL-1 next to cable CBL-3; CB-1 next to the hidden cable CBL-2).

h3. Steps to reproduce
# Open view B on the site above and unlock.
# Select PNL-1 › toolbar Delete › "Delete or Remove?" › Remove from View (screenshot 1): CBL-3 stays.
# Do the same with CB-1, whose cable CBL-2 is hidden (screenshot 2): CBL-2 stays.
# Compare: right-click an asset › Remove from View removes the asset and its cable (screenshot 3).

!QA-12Nov-bugB-2-hidden-cable-left.png|width=640!
_2. After removing CB-1 the same way, its hidden cable CBL-2 stays in the view._

!QA-12Nov-bugB-3-right-click-path-removes-cable.png|width=640!
_3. The right-click path (correct): the asset and its cable both left the view._

h3. Notes for the developer
The toolbar path sends POST /api/sld-view/<view>/nodes/remove with only the selected node id; the right-click path sends the node plus the cable. Found while testing ZP-4947 (re-proved twice: 17:01 and 17:03 IST).

summary: SLD Assemblies: placing the same assembly a second time suggests the name "L1 CB-3" instead of the next name "L2"
desc:
h3. Simple explanation
When a user places a saved assembly on an SLD, the app suggests a name for the new copy.
After placing the first copy as "L1", placing it again should suggest the next free name, for example "L2".
Instead it suggests "L1 CB-3": it takes a device name from the first copy as if it were the copy's name.
If the user accepts the suggestion, the new devices get confusing names such as "QA4942-FDR-L1 CB-3 CB-2". Low priority.

!QA-12Nov-bugC-video-steps.mp4|width=640!
_Video (from the ZP-4942 test): placing the assembly as L1, then the second placement suggesting "L1 CB-3"._

!QA-12Nov-bugC-1-name-suggested-L1-CB-3.png|width=640!
_1. Second placement: the Name box is pre-filled "L1 CB-3" (red box)._

h3. Actual result
The Name box is pre-filled "L1 CB-3", and "Will create" lists "QA4942-FDR-L1 CB-3 CB-2", "QA4942-FDR-L1 CB-3 PNL-2" and so on.

h3. Expected result
The next free copy name, for example "L2" ("Will create QA4942-FDR-L2 CB-2", …). Device names must not be read as copy names.

h3. Test data
* Environment: QA (https://acme.qa.egalvanic.ai), Web v2.6, build index-C1ZRIunF.js, 12 Nov 2026, Super Admin seat.
* Site: "QA-DEMO v2.6 SLD editing 12 Nov" (SLD id c4438cd3-59b3-4639-9e60-2752dc5aa478), Engineering › SLD.
* Assembly "QA4942-FDR-\{name\}" (company-wide, made for the ZP-4942 test). LaunchDarkly feature-sld-assemblies is ON for Acme on QA.

h3. Steps to reproduce
# On the site above, unlock the SLD › + Assembly › pick "QA4942-FDR-\{name\}" › Name "L1" › Place (screenshots 2 and 3).
# Click + Assembly again and pick the same assembly (screenshot 1): the Name box says "L1 CB-3".

!QA-12Nov-bugC-2-first-placement-L1.png|width=640!
_2. First placement: name L1 and the devices it will create._

!QA-12Nov-bugC-3-placed-L1.png|width=640!
_3. The first copy placed as L1._

h3. Notes for the developer
POST /api/assemblies/<id>/place-preview with the SLD id returns "value":"L1 CB-3". Found while testing ZP-4942 (re-proved twice: 16:35 and 16:40 IST, same seat and input).
